title: General Aptitude - Quant, Reasoning, Speed Maths
subtitle: All 30 official areas: percentages to probability, trains to calendars, plus logical reasoning and the five sample puzzles
subtopics: Numbers, Percentage, Ratio, Partnership, Profit-Loss, Discount, Stocks, HCF-LCM
Time-Work, Pipes, Time-Distance, Trains, Boats-Streams, Races

readingSections.title: 1. Numbers, Percent, Ratio, Business Maths (From Zero)
readingSections.quickSummary: Percent means per-hundred. Ratio splits, profit compares to cost, discount compares to marked price. HCF-LCM and digit facts power number questions.
content: Numericals and Numbers: place value, divisibility (2,3,4,5,8,9,11), prime/composite, unit digits. HCF = greatest common divisor (Euclid), LCM = smallest common multiple; for two numbers HCF x LCM = product. Fractions-decimals-percent table: 1/2=50%, 1/3=33.33%, 1/4=25%, 1/5=20%, 1/8=12.5%, 1/10=10%, 1/20=5%.

Percentage: x% of N = xN/100. Change% = (new-old)/old x 100 (base is OLD). Successive a% then b%: net = a+b+ab/100 (signs included). Ratio a:b divides X as aX/(a+b). Proportion a:b::c:d means ad=bc. Partnership profits split by (capital x time) ratios.

Profit-Loss: on COST unless stated. P% = (SP-CP)/CP x 100. Discount on MARKED price: SP = MP(1-d%). True discount = interest on present worth: TD = Amount x rate x time/(100+rate x time); present worth = Amount - TD. Stocks: face value vs market value; dividend% is on FACE; yield = dividend/market x 100.
Worked: cost 800, sold 920: P% = 120/800 = 15%. MP 500, 20% off: SP 400. Two workers (sample): 1/6+1/12 = 1/4 per day, so 4 days together.

subsections.title: Base discipline (the 80% error)
content: Percent base is the OLD/ORIGINAL unless asked otherwise.
Up 25% then down 25% is NOT break-even: 1.25 x 0.75 = 0.9375 (6.25% loss).
Profit on SP vs CP differ - read which the question uses.

subsections.title: HCF-LCM speed
content: HCF by Euclid remainders; LCM by prime powers (max exponents).
Two numbers: product = HCF x LCM (extends only pairwise).
Trailing zeros, bells-together (LCM of periods) are classic frames.

subsections.title: Business chain
content: CP -> (+profit) / (-loss) -> SP; MP -> (-discount) -> SP.
True discount belongs to bills/debts: PW = Amount/(1+rt/100).
Stocks: always convert dividend to yield before comparing.

quickRevision: Percent base is old. Successive: a+b+ab/100.
Profit on CP, discount on MP.
readingSections.companyNote: Percentage-ratio-profit is the densest prelims cluster.

readingSections.title: 2. Work-Time Family - Work, Pipes, Distance, Trains, Boats, Races
readingSections.quickSummary: Work adds rates. Pipes add signed rates. Distance = speed x time with unit discipline. Trains add lengths; boats add/subtract current.
content: Time-Work: rate = 1/days for the whole job. Together: add rates. A(6d)+B(12d): 1/6+1/12 = 1/4, so 4 days (VEDA sample). Man-days = men x days constant for fixed work. Alternate days: pair-cycle method.
Pipes-Cistern: inlet +rate, outlet -rate. Net fills/empties. Leaks subtract. Time to fill with leak: 1/(in - leak).

Time-Distance: D = S x T. Units: km/h x 5/18 = m/s; m/s x 18/5 = km/h. Average speed over equal distances = harmonic 2ab/(a+b), NOT arithmetic mean. Relative speed: towards each other add, same direction subtract.

Trains: train passing object = its length; passing platform/bridge/train = lengths added. VEDA sample: speed 15 m/s, man in 20s gives length 300m; station in 36s gives 540m total, platform 240m. Boats: downstream u+v, upstream u-v (u boat, v stream); still-water speed = (down+up)/2, stream = (down-up)/2. Races: head starts and dead heats read off distance-time graphs; circular tracks meet at LCM of round times.

subsections.title: Unit discipline
content: Convert before computing: km/h to m/s multiply 5/18.
Train seconds x m/s gives metres directly.
Keep days/hours consistent in work-pipe mixes.

example.prompt: Train 15 m/s passes man in 20s. Length?
steps: Point object: length = speed x time.

subsections.title: Rate addition everywhere
content: Workers, pipes, even relative motion all add signed rates.
Together-time = 1/(sum of reciprocals) for two: ab/(a+b).
Outlet/leak/upstream carry minus signs.

subsections.title: Average-speed trap
content: Equal distances at a,b: 2ab/(a+b), always below (a+b)/2.
Equal TIMES average arithmetically - check what is equal.
Races: leader's time decides; lapped meets need LCM.

quickRevision: Together: add reciprocals. ab/(a+b) for two.
km/h to m/s: 5/18. Lengths add for crossings.
readingSections.companyNote: Two train/work samples are official - method must be automatic.

readingSections.title: 3. Averages and Ages
readingSections.quickSummary: Average = total/count. Ages shift together: gaps never change. Weighted average respects group sizes.
content: Average = sum/n. Adding/removing a member: new total = old total +/- value. If average rises by d when a member of value v joins n members: v = old_avg + d(n+1). Weighted average = (n1a1+n2a2)/(n1+n2); mixture age/price problems are weighted averages in disguise.
Ages: difference between two ages is CONSTANT over time. Sum/difference frames solve by equations: present ages x,y; k years ago/hence shift both by k. Ratios of ages at two times give two equations.
x is 80% of y (VEDA sample): x = 0.8y, y/x = 1.25, so y is 1.25/2 = 62.5% of 2x. Read what the percent is OF - the base is 2x here, not y.
Book-price puzzle (VEDA sample): Ram has P-2, Shyam P-24 (integer rupees, both positive), together short: 2P-26 < P gives P < 26; Shyam positive gives P > 24; integer P = 25.

subsections.title: Average-change shortcut
content: New member value = new_avg +/- d x (old count). Sign by rise/fall.
Batsman/cricket averages are the classic frame.
Removing works mirrored: value = old_avg -/+ d x (remaining).

example.prompt: Avg of 10 rises 2 when an 80 joins. Old avg?

subsections.title: Age equations
content: Let present ages be variables; shift both sides equally.
Gap constant: if A-B = 5 now, always 5.
Two time-frames give two equations - solve.

subsections.title: Of-what discipline
content: Percent questions hide the base: underline OF.
x is 80% of y: base y. y as % of 2x: base 2x.
Convert to fractions early (0.8 = 4/5).

quickRevision: Average = total/count. Gaps constant in ages.

readingSections.title: 4. Mensuration, Roots, Logarithms, Height-Distance
readingSections.quickSummary: Area squares length units, volume cubes them. Roots invert powers. Logs turn multiply into add. Height-distance is one tan.
content: Area: rectangle lw, square a2, triangle bh/2, circle pi r2, trapezium h(a+b)/2, sector theta/360 x pi r2. Perimeter/circumference linear in length. Volume: cube a3, cuboid lbh, cylinder pi r2 h, cone pi r2 h/3, sphere 4/3 pi r3, hemisphere 2/3 pi r3. Surface: cube 6a2, cuboid 2(lb+bh+hl), cylinder 2 pi r(h+r) curved 2 pi r h, sphere 4 pi r2.

Square roots: perfect squares to 30 (1,4,9,...,900) plus sqrt2 1.414, sqrt3 1.732. Cube roots of 1,8,27,64,125,216,343,512,729,1000. Simplify radicals: sqrt(72) = 6 sqrt2. Rationalise 1/sqrt2 = sqrt2/2.

Logarithms: log(ab) = log a + log b, log(a/b) = log a - log b, log(a^n) = n log a, log_a(a) = 1, log 1 = 0, change of base log_b(a) = log a/log b. log10(2) = 0.3010, log10(3) = 0.4771 unlock digit counts (digits in 2^10 = floor(10x0.3010)+1 = 4).

Height-Distance: one right triangle, tan = opposite/adjacent. Angle of elevation = looking up, depression = looking down (alternate with elevation from the object). Common: 30/45/60 with tan 1/sqrt3, 1, sqrt3. Shadow = height/tan(elevation).

subsections.title: Unit power check
content: Area in unit2, volume unit3 - mismatch flags formula errors.
Scale: lengths x k gives area x k2, volume x k3.
Pi handling: keep symbolic till the end for exact options.

subsections.title: Log-digit trick
content: Digits in N = floor(log10 N)+1.
Trails zeros in n! need Legendre (beyond scope - skip).

subsections.title: Elevation setup
content: Draw ground, vertical, sight line. Mark known side and angle.
tan ties height to ground distance directly.
Two positions give two equations (tower + walk problems).

quickRevision: Area x k2, volume x k3 on scaling.
readingSections.companyNote: Formula breadth beats depth here - memorise the table.

readingSections.title: 5. Counting, Probability, Logical Reasoning (Official Samples Inside)
readingSections.quickSummary: Arrange with factorial, choose with combinations. Probability = good/total. Venn: add both, subtract overlap thrice-counted.
content: Permutations nPr = n!/(n-r)! (order matters: seats, ranks, codes without repeat). Combinations nCr = n!/(r!(n-r)!) (order free: teams, hands). nCr = nC(n-r). Circular seats: (n-1)!. Repeated letters divide by repeats. AND means multiply (sequential choices), OR across exclusive cases means add.

Probability = favourable/possible (equally likely). Complement P(not) = 1-P. Independent AND multiplies, mutually-exclusive OR adds. Dice/cards/coins/balls-without-replacement are the four frames. Conditional P(A|B) = P(AB)/P(B).

Logical reasoning VEDA set, all solved: (1) Venn jobs: 90 total, 10 neither, so 80 in circle(s); 65+58 = 123 counts both twice, overlap = 123-80 = 43. (2) Workers 6/12 days: 1/6+1/12 = 1/4, so 4 days. (3) Book Rs 25 (shown in Ages section). (4) Train platform 240m (shown in Trains). (5) 62.5% (shown in Percent). General Venn: |A u B| = |A|+|B|-|AB|; three-set adds triple back once.
Reasoning tactics: draw the Venn, write equations for unknowns, extreme-case test (all/none overlap) to bound answers, verify totals sum to universe.

subsections.title: Choose vs arrange test
content: Labels/positions/ranks differ: permute.
Mere membership: combine.
Mixed: choose then arrange (committees with posts).

subsections.title: Probability frames
content: Dice: 36 pairs. Cards: 52 (26 red, 4 suits). Coins: 2^n.
Without replacement: denominators shrink.
At-least-one via complement: 1 - P(none).

subsections.title: Venn in 20 seconds
content: Neither-outside first: inside = total - neither.
Sum of circles minus inside = overlap.
Only-A = A minus overlap.

quickRevision: nPr orders, nCr chooses. AND-multiply, OR-add.

readingSections.title: 6. Calendar, Clock, Stocks Wrap, Speed Tactics
readingSections.quickSummary: Odd days mod 7 drive calendars. Clock hands move 360/12/720. Stocks compare yield, not dividend. In the hall: decimals last, triples first.
content: Calendar: ordinary year 365 = 52 weeks + 1 odd day; leap 366 = +2. Century odd days: 100 (5), 200 (3), 300 (1), 400 (0, repeats every 400 years). Month codes via odd days (Jan 3 in ordinary/4 in leap, Feb 0/1, Mar 3, Apr 6, May 1, Jun 4, Jul 6, Aug 2, Sep 5, Oct 0, Nov 3, Dec 5). Day = (year odd + month odd + date) mod 7 (0 Sunday). Leap if divisible by 4, except centuries need 400.

Clock: minute hand 360 deg/hour (6/min), hour hand 30 deg/hour (0.5/min), relative 5.5 deg/min. Angle = |30H - 5.5M|. Coincide every 65 5/11 min (~12/11 h). Right angles twice hourly (except 2-4 band quirks), opposite once hourly. Gains/losses scale indicated vs true time.
Stocks wrap: dividend% on face; price is market; yield decides. Buy low-yield? No - buy HIGH yield (more dividend per rupee). Brokerage adds to cost.

Tactics: attempt order - Venn/percent/average first (fast), trains/work next, P&C/probability with diagrams, calendars/clocks by formula, mensuration by table lookup. Keep fraction-decimal-percent table on rough sheet. Never linear-add RMS-like or rate quantities - pause and check the operation.

subsections.title: Odd-day arithmetic
content: Everything mod 7. Leap adds one extra day after Feb.
2000 was leap (400 rule); 1900 was not.
Same calendar repeats with same Jan-1 weekday + leap match.

subsections.title: Clock angle drill
content: |30H - 5.5M|, take smaller with 360 if needed.
3:00 gives 90 exactly.
Coincidence ~ every 1h05m.

subsections.title: Yield comparison
content: Rs 100 at 60 (8% dividend): yield 8/60 = 13.3%.
Rs 100 at 120 (8%): yield 6.7%. Same dividend, worse buy.
Face is for dividend, market is for money.
